public_rationale: The claim is that adding vision to LLMs had not solved hallucinations as of April 2024. OpenAI's own system card for GPT-4V (September 2023) says the model 'was prone to hallucinations' and made factual errors in an authoritative tone. HallusionBench, a CVPR 2024 benchmark whose latest version came out in March 2024, tested 15 vision-language models, including GPT-4V, Gemini Pro Vision and Claude 3. The best model reached only 31.42% question-pair accuracy, and the paper documents hallucination failures. A survey posted two weeks after the post also calls multimodal hallucination frequent and unsolved. No source from the period claims the problem was solved. The claim is supported.
limitations: 'Solved' is undefined. The claim is read as hallucinations remaining a material problem. Some reduction in hallucination rates did occur during the period.
Benchmarks are built to be hard, so their accuracy figures overstate everyday error rates. Still, the developer's own disclosure independently confirms that hallucinations persisted.

statement.document_title: TED, AI, and the test of time

from_speaker: stated in April 2024, looking back on the year since TED 2023
our_interpretation: Plain reading: the multimodal (vision-plus-language) models released between TED 2023 and the post, such as GPT-4V, Gemini Pro Vision and Claude 3, still produced hallucinations often enough to be a recognized, documented problem.

'Solved' means hallucinations were no longer a material problem. Showing that leading models still hallucinated in documented evaluations is enough to support the claim. The claim does not say visual data made no improvement at all.
Target period: from TED 2023 (April 2023) to the post date (2024-04-15).
criteria.support_condition: Developer documentation or published evaluations from the period show that leading multimodal LLMs still hallucinated in material ways.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence from the period shows that leading multimodal LLMs had essentially eliminated hallucinations, or that adding vision had been shown to resolve them.
